def revcomp(s):

def fold(seq):

unit_tgt='((((((((..((((....))))..((((....))))..((((....))))..((((....))))..))))))))'

inner1=d['inner1']; found=d['found1']

def graft(inner, outer5):
    return outer5+inner+revcomp(outer5)

# A unit's 5'stem=outer5, 3'stem=revcomp(outer5).
# Cross-pair between unit_i(5') and unit_j(3'): need revcomp(unit_i.outer5) == unit_j's 3'stem read = revcomp(unit_j.outer5)
# i.e. revcomp(oi) == revcomp(oj) -> oi==oj. With distinct ois, perfect cross-pair 5'i-3'j needs oi==oj (same). 
# But PARTIAL cross-pairing (wobbles/mismatches) can still form a helix. To minimize, pick stems where oi and oj are very different (low complementarity).
# Stronger: ensure oi is not complementary to revcomp(oj) at many positions. oi vs revcomp(oj): pairing oi[k] with revcomp(oj)[7-k].
# Actually the dangerous pairing: oi[k] pairs oj's 3'stem position. unit_j 3'stem = revcomp(oj), positions 66..73 = revcomp(oj)[0..7] = oj reversed+complemented.
# unit_i 5'stem oi at pos 0..7. Pairing i 5'(k) with j 3'(73-k): 
#   j[73-k] = revcomp(oj)[7-k] = comp(oj[k]). So i[k] pairs comp(oj[k]).
#   Valid pair iff oi[k] complements comp(oj[k]) iff oi[k]==oj[k] (since comp(comp(x))=x, need oi[k]=oj[k]).
# Wait that means PERFECT cross-pair needs oi==oj. Distinct ois avoid perfect. 
# For PARTIAL: count positions where oi[k] complements j's corresponding base.
# j 3'stem pos (73-k) base = revcomp(oj)[7-k]. oi[k] pairs it iff oi[k] complements revcomp(oj)[7-k].
# revcomp(oj)[7-k] = comp(oj[k]). oi[k] complements comp(oj[k]) means oi[k]==oj[k].
# So cross-pairing strength = number of positions where oi[k]==oj[k]. Pick stems with LOW positional identity!

# Greedy: pick 5 stems minimizing max pairwise positional-equal count.
def paircross(a,b):
    # number of positions where a[k]==b[k] (perfect cross-pair positions)
    return sum(1 for k in range(8) if a[k]==b[k])

# sort found by GC richness (prefer GC)
